questions.q: The chapter's patch priority score is computed as:
options: (CVSS base score × 10) × (1 + EPSS score) × exposure multiplier, capped at 100
CVSS base score + EPSS score + number of affected instances
The maximum CVSS base score among all published CVEs for the product
A fixed 0–100 value assigned manually by the security team per bulletin
questions.explain: compute_priority_score multiplies (cvss_score * 10) by (1 + epss_score) by an exposure multiplier derived from affected instance count, capped at 100.

questions.q: A patch classified as Tier 1 (priority score ≥ 80) is handled how?
options: Deployed within 24 hours, bypassing the standard change freeze
Deployed within the next scheduled maintenance window (≤ 7 days)
Batched with the next planned minor version upgrade
Queued for manual CAB review before any rollout
questions.explain: The chapter defines Tier 1 (score ≥ 80) as deploy within 24 hours and bypassing the standard change freeze; Tier 2 goes to the next window and Tier 3 batches.

questions.q: In the staged rollout model, what defines Ring 2?
options: Dev/test clusters with a 2-hour dwell time
Production canary — 1 cluster, 48-hour dwell, evaluated on all Ring 1 metrics plus replication lag
Staging clusters taking 10% of traffic with a 24-hour dwell
Production batch rolled out at 25% per wave with 72 hours per wave
questions.explain: The ring table lists Ring 2 as the production canary (1 cluster) with 48-hour dwell and pass criteria of all Ring 1 metrics plus replication lag.

questions.q: In the AG patch-gate validation query, which condition produces a WARN patch_gate_status?
options: synchronization_health_desc is not 'HEALTHY'
redo_queue_size exceeds 51200 or secondary_lag_seconds exceeds 30
Any replica returns is_local = 1 instead of 0
log_send_queue_size is non-zero on any secondary
questions.explain: The CASE in the validation query returns 'WARN' when redo_queue_size > 51200 or secondary_lag_seconds > 30, and 'FAIL' when health is not HEALTHY.

questions.q: What is the correct zero-downtime patch sequence for a SQL Server Always On Availability Group per the chapter?
options: Patch the primary first, failover, then patch all secondaries simultaneously
Take a full backup, patch all replicas at once, then verify with DBCC CHECKDB
Patch secondary replicas first and verify re-synchronization, move the primary role with ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP ... FAILOVER, then patch the former primary
Failover to a secondary, patch every node, failover back, with no validation in between
questions.explain: The chapter's AG patch sequencer patches secondaries first, verifies they re-synchronize, issues ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP ... FAILOVER to a patched replica, then patches the old primary.
